tasks.name: partial-degrade-build
tasks.title: One failing language must never abort the whole index build
tasks.goal: Make `internal/index` degrade per-language instead of collapsing. Today `buildAtLayout` (internal/index/builder.go) aborts and writes no manifest when every indexer fails, and — worse — a single `scip.Parse` failure at builder.go:317 returns an error for the entire build, discarding the languages that succeeded and leaving the previous stale manifest untouched. Fix both: a per-language parse/ingest failure must be recorded as an `IndexerFailed` result for that language while every other language still ingests, and a manifest must be written on every build that produced any usable output (status `partial`). Only a genuinely untrustworthy outcome — storage dir uncreatable, store un-openable, `Reset` failure, manifest unwritable — may abort. When zero languages produced output, still write a manifest recording every language's failure plus remedy rather than returning bare `rpc error -32603` with no manifest. Also record per-language ingest counts on `IndexerResult` (documents, symbols, definitions, references) so downstream consumers can tell a language that indexed nothing from one that indexed nothing because it never ran. Cover with table-driven tests through the injected `run func(language string) error` seam in `buildResults` plus a `buildAtLayout`-level test using a fake/stubbed indexer runner — no test may require scip-typescript, scip-python, scip-go, php, or npm on PATH.
tasks.interfaces: `index.IndexerResult` (internal/index/result.go) gains four int fields, all `omitempty`, all zero for non-`ok` statuses: `DocumentCount int \`json:"document_count,omitempty"\``, `SymbolCount int \`json:"symbol_count,omitempty"\``, `DefinitionCount int \`json:"definition_count,omitempty"\``, `ReferenceCount int \`json:"reference_count,omitempty"\``. These are populated from the per-language `scip.Stats` returned by `scip.Parse`, before aggregation into `Manifest.Stats`. `IndexerFailed` remains the status used for a language whose parse step failed, with `Error` carrying the wrapped parse error. `deriveStatus` semantics are unchanged: any primary language in `missing`/`failed` => `partial`, else `ready`. Do NOT add a stderr field (owned by indexer-stderr-capture) and do NOT add staleness/empty fields to `Manifest` (owned by stale-and-empty-signals).

tasks.name: indexer-stderr-capture
tasks.title: Capture and surface the indexer's actual stderr, not just 'exit status 1'
tasks.goal: `scip-typescript exited non-zero: exit status 1` is the entire diagnostic a user gets today. Change each shell-out indexer in `internal/sources/typescript`, `internal/sources/golang`, `internal/sources/php`, and `internal/sources/python` to capture the child process's stderr and, on non-zero exit, return an error carrying a clipped tail of it (last ~8 KB — the tail is where the compiler's real complaint lands; prepend an explicit truncation marker when clipping). Introduce one shared error type for this so `errors.As` works uniformly, keep existing not-found sentinels (`typescript.ErrIndexerNotFound` etc.) matchable via `errors.Is` so `index.classify` still routes them to `missing`. Then record the captured tail on `IndexerResult` and surface it through `scry status` (daemon `StatusResult`, internal/daemon/methods.go) and `scry doctor` (internal/doctor) — full tail in `--json`, a clipped few lines in the human checklist with a pointer to the JSON for the rest. Tests must exercise capture and clipping without any real indexer binary: run a fake command (e.g. a `sh -c` or `go run`-free stub, or inject the exec seam) that writes a large known stderr and exits non-zero, and assert the tail, the truncation marker, and that the sentinel classification is preserved.
tasks.interfaces: New exported type in a shared location (suggest `internal/sources/scip` or a small `internal/sources/exec` helper): `type ExitError struct { Tool string; Err error; Stderr string }` with `Error() string` rendering `"<tool> exited non-zero: <err>: <last line of stderr>"` and `Unwrap() error`. `index.IndexerResult` (internal/index/result.go) gains `Stderr string \`json:"stderr,omitempty"\``, populated by `classify` via `errors.As` on the runner error; `classify`'s signature becomes `classify(language string, err error) (status, errMsg, remedy, stderr string)` — update its single caller in `buildResults`. Cap the persisted tail at 8192 bytes; when clipped, the string starts with `"...[truncated, showing last 8192 bytes]\n"`. `daemon.StatusResult` per-repo entries and `doctor` JSON output pass this field through verbatim under key `stderr`.

tasks.name: npm-indexer-provisioning
tasks.title: Provision npm-published indexers from `scry install` and `scry doctor --fix`
tasks.goal: `internal/install/install.go` documents that scip-typescript has no GitHub release assets and therefore skips it, handing the user a remedy string to run by hand; scip-python has the same problem. Both install cleanly from npm (`npm i -g @sourcegraph/scip-typescript` → 0.4.0, `npm i -g @sourcegraph/scip-python`). Add an npm provisioning path: detect npm on PATH, install the package globally, verify the resulting binary is invocable, and report what happened. When npm is absent, do not silently skip — emit the exact command the user must run and the prerequisite that is missing. Wire this into both `scry install` and `scry doctor --fix` (internal/doctor/fix.go) so a single command can bring a broken machine to green. Also handle the specific case that burned the reproduction: a daemon started before the install has a stale PATH and will keep reporting the tool as missing forever. Detect it — the binary resolves for the CLI process but the daemon's recorded environment/start time predates the install — and say so explicitly ('scip-typescript is installed but the running daemon started before it; run `scry daemon restart`') rather than reporting the tool as missing. Structure the provisioning decision as a pure, table-testable function; no test may shell out to npm or require any indexer installed.
tasks.interfaces: New in `internal/install`: `type Source int` with constants `SourceGitHubRelease`, `SourceNPM`, `SourceManual`; `type Plan struct { Tool string; Source Source; Package string; Command []string; Reason string; Actionable bool }`; and the pure decision function `func PlanFor(tool string, env Env) Plan` where `type Env struct { NPMPath string; ToolPath string; DaemonStartedAt time.Time; ToolInstalledAt time.Time }` — all inputs injected, nothing probed inside. `PlanFor` returns `Actionable:false` with a `Reason` naming the missing prerequisite when `NPMPath` is empty. A separate `func StaleDaemonPATH(env Env) bool` returns true when `ToolPath != ""` && `!DaemonStartedAt.IsZero()` && `ToolInstalledAt.After(DaemonStartedAt)`; doctor renders that as a WARN with the restart remedy, never as a FAIL/missing. Tool keys are the same strings used by `index.indexerRemedies`: `typescript`, `python`, `go`, `php`.

tasks.name: stale-and-empty-signals
tasks.title: Detect and report stale and empty indexes instead of a silent green
tasks.goal: A repo indexed months ago and a repo whose graph builds `node_count: 0, edge_count: 0` from a non-empty file set both report `ready` today. Add two derived signals. STALE: the index is older than the repo's current HEAD — compare the manifest's `IndexedAt`/recorded HEAD against the live HEAD via the existing `internal/git` helpers; if HEAD moved (or, when HEAD is unavailable, the newest source file mtime is newer than `IndexedAt`), mark stale. Record the HEAD commit at build time in the manifest so the comparison is exact rather than clock-based. EMPTY: a primary language whose indexer reported `ok` but produced zero symbols across a non-zero detected file count is a failure wearing a success label — flag it per-language and roll it up to the repo. Surface both through `scry status` (daemon `StatusResult`) and `scry doctor`: a repo can be `ready`, `partial`, `stale`, or `empty`, and doctor must print which languages are empty and how old the index is. Neither signal may require a reindex to compute, and neither may make `scry status` slow — HEAD resolution is one git call per repo, cached for the status call. Tests must cover: HEAD-moved stale, HEAD-unchanged not-stale, missing-git fallback, empty-with-files flagged, empty-with-no-files not flagged, and the precedence order when a repo is both partial and stale.
tasks.interfaces: Consumes `IndexerResult.SymbolCount`/`FileCount` from partial-degrade-build for the empty check. `index.Manifest` gains `HeadCommit string \`json:"head_commit,omitempty"\`` (recorded at build time; empty when the repo is not a git checkout). New exported helpers in `internal/index`: `func IsStale(m *Manifest, currentHead string, newestSourceMTime time.Time) bool` and `func EmptyLanguages(m *Manifest) []string` (primary languages with `Status == IndexerOK && SymbolCount == 0 && FileCount > 0`). `Manifest.Status` on disk keeps only `ready`/`partial` — `stale` and `empty` are DERIVED at report time and never written to the manifest, so a stale index does not need rewriting to be diagnosed. The daemon exposes them as additive fields on each repo entry in `StatusResult`: `stale bool`, `empty_languages []string`, and a display-only `effective_status string` with precedence `partial > empty > stale > ready`.
